selected_scope: Only exact pointwise reconstruction of one first-order query, Appendix B.1 primitive definition and Ex33–35, interpreted using the actual Section 2 quadratic oracle and Section 3 E4/E5 precision. No adaptive transcript or full lower-bound certification.

objects.statement: Euclidean real vectors and real matrices; O(n) consists of n by n real matrices O with transpose(O) O = I_n.

A_O = ((κ+1)/2) I_n - ((κ-1)/4)(O+transpose(O)); the actual full precision is A_boldO = diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_(d-kn)). These are concrete matrices, not arbitrary block operators supplied by a query evaluator.

The potential is f_A(x) = (1/2) x^T A x, and exact FO_A(x) is the ordered value-and-gradient pair ((1/2)x^T A x, A x). The source target is the centered Gaussian N(0,A^{-1}), but no distributional conclusion is selected here.
Primitive oracle O_boldO(j,v,f) = O_j v; O_boldO(j,v,i) = transpose(O_j) v. Inverse means transpose of this orthogonal block.
Query x=(x_1,...,x_k,z); each unknown block contributes g_j=((κ+1)/2)x_j-((κ-1)/4)(F_j+I_j), where F_j and I_j are the actual forward and inverse responses at the same input x_j.

domains.statement: The Section 2 model has integer d≥1, real κ≥1, and A symmetric with I_d ⪯ A ⪯ κ I_d; x ranges over all R^d.
The selected hard-family construction stands at κ≥4, integer block dimension 3≤n≤d, k=floor(d/n), and tuple (O_1,...,O_k) in O(n)^k. Consequently d-kn is a nonnegative integer.
j ranges over {1,...,k}; primitive v and every x_j lie in R^n; z lies in R^(d-kn); τ has the two meaningful tags forward f and inverse i.

When kn=d, the identity block is omitted. The pointwise formula then has no residual coordinates; equivalently a zero-dimensional residual contributes the unique empty vector and zero inner-product term.

quantifiers.statement: For every source-admissible κ,d,n and associated k, for every tuple of orthogonal blocks, for every point x=(x_1,...,x_k,z), and for each j=1,...,k, the displayed reconstruction equalities hold exactly. The oracle responses are fixed by those blocks and inputs; they are not independently chosen witnesses.

The pointwise equalities do not quantify over algorithms, seeds, transcripts, priors, stopping times, or target samples. Repeating a pointwise evaluator at T queries explains the local resource count, but adaptive law equality is a further argument outside this selection.

assumptions.statement: SOURCE/STANDING: the actual hard-family precision uses exactly E4/E5 and orthogonal blocks in the source parameter regime. TYPING: real finite Euclidean coordinates, their dimensions, ordinary inner product, transpose and matrix multiplication.
Exact oracle access: responses are precisely O_j x_j and transpose(O_j) x_j; no error, randomness, approximation tolerance, or noisy observations appear in the selected identities.

Appendix B.1 has the ambient condition 2T<n. It is used by the ensuing indistinguishability proof, not by the algebraic reconstruction equations Ex33–35. Likewise k=floor(d/n), n≥3, κ≥4 and orthogonality specify the source family, though the displayed matrix algebra extends beyond several of those restrictions. Such an extension should be identified as an algebraic generalization, not as a source repair.

No extra nonzero-vector, positive residual dimension, sign-specific determinant, Haar-randomness, Borelness, probability independence, spectral-bound witness, or pre-assumed reconstruction conclusion is required to establish these pointwise algebraic identities. The broader algorithm model has Borel requirements, but these are not additional premises of this selected pointwise result.

conclusion.statement: The actual gradient of f_(A_boldO) is (A_O1 x_1,...,A_Ok x_k,z), which is reconstructed as (g_1,...,g_k,z). The identity residual passes through unchanged.

The actual function value is (1/2)〈x,∇f_(A_boldO)(x)〉; hence the evaluator returns exactly the source FO ordered pair (value,gradient). In block coordinates the value is (1/2)(sum_j〈x_j,g_j〉+〈z,z〉). The expanded block expression is a consequence, not an extra source quotation.

One point needs at most two primitive queries per block: the forward and inverse responses at x_j. This is 2k primitive queries across all k blocks, with no primitive query on the identity residual and no further oracle query for the value.

scopes.statement: Equality is deterministic, pointwise and exact on the whole source query domain, not almost everywhere, in probability, in expectation, or only on nonzero vectors.

The pair has the Section 2 meaning: actual quadratic value and actual gradient/matrix-vector product for E4/E5. Equality to a separately invented response function without this connection would leave an unproved semantic bridge.
The resource phrase is per block. Two calls total for all k unknown blocks is not the selected source assertion.

The last sentence of the Oracle reduction paragraph also claims sufficiency of adaptive primitive transcript indistinguishability when 2T<n. This phase does not certify that adaptive reduction, its measurability, conditional Haar laws, Lemma 3.2, or the Gaussian sampling lower bound.
The zero-residual convention is literal omission or its zero-dimensional Euclidean encoding; the z entry is not an extra unknown hard block.

constant_dependencies.statement: The reconstruction coefficients are exactly c=(κ+1)/2 and a=(κ-1)/4, shared by all blocks; gradient uses c x_j - a(F_j+I_j), and value uses the exact scalar 1/2. They depend only on κ.

The resource bound is the absolute count two per block per point, hence at most 2T per block over T points. k enters only the total count 2k per point and number of coordinates; d-kn fixes residual dimension. There are no hidden constants or dependence on x,O_j,determinant sign,ε,or a probability event.
n=2T+1 and 2T<n belong to the later lower-bound/indistinguishability application; they are not coefficient constraints or denominator conditions in Ex33–35.

verdict: No candidate verdict in phase 1. This is an independently frozen source baseline.
